The submitted answer is 0, and I could not verify it.

Adding the three equations gives x² + y² + z² + 6x − 2y − 4z = −14. Completing the squares turns this into (x+3)² + (y−1)² + (z−2)² = 0. The only real candidate is therefore (x, y, z) = (−3, 1, 2), which gives xy + xz + 6yz = −3 − 6 + 12 = 3.

That triple fails the first equation, since x² − 2y = 9 − 2 = 7, not −13. So the system as stated has no real solution, and the intended answer from the sum-of-squares method is 3.

The program output lists eight complex solutions. None of them gives xy + xz + 6yz = 0; the values are all different and none is 0. So 0 is not supported on either reading.
